state.misconception_label: Does not understand that 2n represents an even number

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: Which of these shows part of the proof that the sum of two odd numbers is even? I got \( \begin{array}{l}2 n+(2 m+1) \\ =2(n+m)+1\end{array} \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me explain the correct method, and then we will work through an example together. So, when we have 2n, it represents an even number because it can be divided by 2 evenly. Let's work through an example to make this clearer. Let's say n is 3, so 2n would be 6, which is an even number. Can you see why 2n represents an even number now?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, yeah I see that 2n = 6 when n is 3, so it's even because you can divide it by 2. But then... if 2n is even, why did I write 2n at the start of my answer? Shouldn't I have written something different for an odd number?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me explain the correct method, and then we will work through an example together. So, when we use 2n in our equation, it represents an even number. In this case, 2n is added to an odd number to show that the sum is even. Can you see how that works now?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, I'm a bit confused though... if 2n is even, then how does adding it to an odd number make the answer even? Wouldn't even plus odd equal odd? And also, shouldn't I have used 2n+1 for the odd number instead of just 2n?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher repeatedly explains rather than engaging with the student's emerging understanding, provides mathematically confused explanations about adding even and odd numbers, and the student ends more confused than at the start, now questioning basic facts about even+odd and showing they haven't grasped how to represent odd numbers.
score.justification_pass2: While the teacher attempts to use worked examples (n=3), they fail to provide clear, comprehensive explanations of the core concept (representing odd numbers as 2n+1), repeat vague explanations without addressing the student's valid confusion, and don't correct the fundamental misconception about the algebraic representation of odd numbers.
